subject: maths
title: Trig Tower
description: Differentiate sin x from first principles using key limits.

concepts.def: sin(x+h) = sin x cos h + cos x sin h.
= sin x (cos h − 1)/h + cos x (sin h)/h.
Limit gives cos x, so d/dx(sin x) = cos x.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Use sin(x+h) expansion

Take limit using lim sin h/h = 1 and (cos h -1)/h = 0 = cos x

Similar method using cos(x+h)=cos x cos h − sin x sin h

Apply key limits = −sin x

options: h
cos x
-sin x
-cos x
sin x
1 for all x — the Pythagorean trigonometric identity.
Sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) equals x because the trig functions cancel.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
Sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) depends on x and varies between 0 and 2.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of a constant, like d/dx(5)?
options: 0 — constants do not change with x.
The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
Sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) depends on x and varies between 0 and 2.
The derivative of 5 is 5 because the constant stays the same.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of (3x + 1)^2 with respect to x?
options: The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
The derivative is 2(3x + 1) — applying the power rule without the chain rule.
6(3x + 1) — by the chain rule, multiplying by the derivative of the inside (3).

f(x)=sin x: [sin(x+h)−sin x]/h.
